_spec: BANZA Conformance Profiles L0–L4 — Normative Registry
_authority: This registry. It is the single normative definition of what each conformance profile requires. docs/governance/certification-boundary.md explains these profiles for a human reader and MUST agree with this file; where the two differ, this file governs and the prose is the defect.
_boundary: A profile states what an implementation must satisfy to claim that level. It confers nothing: no certification, no admission, no authorisation, and no permission to operate. Levels denote conformance readiness only (ADR-021, ADR-060, ADR-061).
_derivation: The capability, invariant and asset lists are the corrected per-level model of ADR-021. Every invariant id here exists in contracts/invariants.json; every vector and suite path here exists in conformance/. A guard enforces both, so this registry cannot drift from the material it references.
_cumulative_note: Each profile INCLUDES every requirement of the profiles it lists in `includes`. The `required_*` members of a profile are its INCREMENT — what that level adds. An implementation's full obligation at level N is the transitive closure over `includes`. Cumulative does not mean 'concatenate directories': the closure is computed over these declared members only.

profiles.name: Protocol Sandbox
profiles.purpose: Prove the protocol can be instantiated in a controlled test environment and that the core monetary representation is correct.
not_required: Live payment rails of any kind
Wallets, transfers or a ledger — those are L1
Payment requests, QR or instant execution — those are L2
Federation, cross-operator routing or settlement — those are L3
External payment-network integration — that is L4
Trust material of your own: no signing key, no key manifest, no published metadata. L0 needs no identity and no signature
Any registration, submission, approval or credential from any party
profiles._note: L0 is deliberately the smallest complete statement of the protocol: represent money as integers correctly, produce a valid manifest, canonicalize deterministically, and use published reason codes. It is exercised locally; nothing is issued to anyone.

profiles.name: Core Payment Capability
profiles.purpose: Consumer payment, merchant acceptance, transfer and traceability capability.
not_required: Payment requests, dynamic QR or instant execution — those are L2
Any federation capability — that is L3
profiles._note: Traceability is L1, not L2. The superseded mapping that placed it at L2 was corrected by ADR-021.

profiles.name: Payment Initiation Capability
profiles.purpose: Payment request, payment initiation and instant execution capability.
not_required: Cross-operator routing, reconciliation or inter-operator settlement — those are L3
Published signed protocol metadata — first required at L3
profiles._note: Payment initiation — payment requests, dynamic QR, instant execution — is L2, not L1.

profiles.name: Inter-Operator Interoperability
profiles.purpose: Cross-operator routing, inter-operator settlement and automated reconciliation. This is the federation eligibility threshold.
required_publication: Operator manifest declaring supports_federation and cross_operator_routing, served at the implementation's own well-known location
L3 conformance evidence bundle consistent with the manifest
profiles._not_awarded_reason: L3 requires evidence produced by two independent implementations. A single-implementation run cannot produce it, so no sandbox runner awards this level.
not_required: External payment-network integration — that is L4
Any certificate issued by any party: trust is evaluated from published material, there is no BANZA CA and no operator certificate

profiles.name: External Interoperability
profiles.purpose: Integration with external payment networks and acquiring infrastructure.
profiles._not_awarded_reason: External-rail acquiring cannot be proven against a simulated environment. L4 is profile-defined and requires external integration evidence.
not_required: Any universal implementation artifact beyond L3 — L4 adds none, and this is a property of the level rather than a gap in this registry
A profile invented for the purpose: an L4 claim names a real external profile or it is not an L4 claim
profiles._note: No production external-rail integration is claimed in this repository. This profile states the MECHANISM by which L4 is claimed and demonstrated; nothing here demonstrates it.

external_profile._semantics: L4 inherits every L3 requirement and introduces NO universal implementation artifact of its own. Its additional requirements are supplied by the external-interoperability profile an implementation selects. Zero universal artifacts therefore does NOT make L4 equivalent to L3: an implementation that satisfies L3 has satisfied none of L4's profile-supplied requirements, because it has selected no profile.
must_identify: The external network or acquiring infrastructure being integrated with
The external-interoperability profile the integration is claimed against, by identifier and version
The scope of the claim: L4 is demonstrated FOR that profile, never in general
must_evidence: Evidence of the external integration itself, satisfying the selected profile
The L3 evidence L4 inherits, unchanged

demonstrability._scope: A property of the selected external profile, NOT a universal property of L4. Whether an integration can be demonstrated without touching the live external network depends on what that profile accepts as evidence, and a profile may legitimately define evidence producible in a test or sandbox environment where the external counterparty is represented faithfully enough. BANZA 1.0.0 makes no universal ruling either way, because it has no basis for one.
demonstrability.current_state: No concrete external-interoperability profile is published, so BANZA 1.0.0 has no executable L4 demonstration. This is a statement about what exists today, not about what is possible.

external_profile._result_vocabulary: `not_run` is the per-level result vocabulary already published in contracts/production/conformance-report.production.schema.json. It is the correct outcome here and `fail` is not: nothing failed. It is not `not_applicable` either: L4 applies, and was not evaluated because no profile was selected and no external evidence supplied.
external_profile._published_profiles_note: EMPTY, and stated rather than concealed. No concrete external-interoperability profile is published in BANZA 1.0.0, and none is invented here to make the mechanism look exercised. The L4 mechanism is defined; no L4 profile or evidence currently exists, which is consistent with a pre-production protocol.

non_profile_artifacts._why: An artifact on the normative surface that no profile requires is not automatically surplus. Two classes below are required by nobody implementing a level, for reasons that are properties of the artifact rather than gaps in this registry. Declaring them here is what makes the remaining orphans meaningful: anything outside these lists that no profile requires is a defect to be resolved, not noise to be tolerated.

evidence_and_record_structures.reason: These define the SHAPE OF AN OUTPUT — a report, a record, a release — produced about an implementation once it has been evaluated. An implementer does not implement them to reach a level; a party reading the evidence parses them. Placing them in a profile would tell an implementer to build the report about itself.

trust_root_operation.reason: These constrain how the BANZA Trust Root itself is operated — custody, ceremony, backup, recovery, revocation of the root. They bind the party holding the root, not any implementation of the protocol. No conformance level requires an implementer to perform a root ceremony, and a profile that demanded it would be asking implementers to become the trust root.

profile_registry_itself.reason: The profile registry and its schema define the profiles; a profile cannot require the document that defines it without circularity. They are on the normative surface and are read by anyone determining a level, but they are not implemented at a level.
